goals: Describe Bose's early career and his two Congress presidencies
Explain why he resigned in 1939 and formed the Forward Bloc
State the objectives of the Forward Bloc

slides.heading: A leader in a hurry for freedom
slides.body_md: Part 1 — Bose's **early career**, **Haripura and Tripuri**, and the **Forward Bloc**.

slides.narration: Subhas Chandra Bose, remembered as Netaji, wanted India to win full freedom without delay. In this part we follow his early career, his two terms as Congress President, the crisis at Tripuri in nineteen thirty-nine, and the new group he then formed, the Forward Bloc. In Part Two we follow him abroad and to the Indian National Army.

slides.narration: This timeline gives the main dates of the chapter. Bose was born in eighteen ninety-seven and left the civil service in nineteen twenty-one. He presided at Haripura in nineteen thirty-eight and formed the Forward Bloc in nineteen thirty-nine. He escaped in nineteen forty-one. The first army came in nineteen forty-two, the Provisional Government in nineteen forty-three, and the Red Fort trials in nineteen forty-five.

slides.narration: Bose was born at Cuttack in eighteen ninety-seven. He passed the Indian Civil Service examination in nineteen twenty, but resigned the next year because he did not wish to serve the colonial government. He joined the national movement in Bengal under C. R. Das, became a leader of the youth, and was imprisoned several times by the British.

slides.heading: Haripura and Tripuri
slides.body_md: **1938** at Haripura; **1939** re-elected for Tripuri.

rows: Bose presides; presses for a firmer struggle; National Planning Committee set up
Re-elected over Pattabhi Sitaramayya; senior leaders do not cooperate; resigns

visual.alt: Table of Bose's two Congress presidencies: Haripura in 1938, where he pressed for a firmer struggle and the National Planning Committee was set up; and Tripuri in 1939, where he was re-elected over Pattabhi Sitaramayya but resigned when senior leaders did not cooperate

slides.narration: In nineteen thirty-eight Bose presided over the Congress session at Haripura. He pressed for a firmer struggle against British rule, and the National Planning Committee was set up during his term. In nineteen thirty-nine he stood again and defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate backed by Gandhi and many senior leaders. This victory led to a crisis.

slides.heading: The Tripuri crisis
slides.body_md: Re-elected, but **unable to form a team**: he **resigns**.

nodes.label: Senior leaders who backed the rival do not join his working committee
Differences over the pace of the struggle
May 1939: Forward Bloc formed within the Congress

visual.alt: Flow of the Tripuri crisis: Bose defeats Pattabhi Sitaramayya in 1939; senior leaders do not join his working committee; differences over the pace of the struggle; Bose resigns; in May 1939 he forms the Forward Bloc within the Congress
visual.caption: From victory to a new group.

slides.narration: After the election, senior leaders who had backed his rival would not join his working committee, and Bose differed with them on how hard to press the British. Unable to function as President, he resigned in nineteen thirty-nine. He then formed a new group, the Forward Bloc, at first within the Congress itself.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: explaining the resignation
slides.body_md: Explain in **two points** why Bose resigned in 1939.
bullets: Point 1: senior leaders who backed **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** did **not cooperate** in forming a working committee.
Point 2: he **differed** with them on the **pace** of the struggle.
Tip: keep the tone **neutral**; describe the disagreement, do not take sides.

slides.narration: For a two-mark answer on the resignation, give two distinct points. First, the senior leaders who had supported his rival did not cooperate in forming a working committee. Second, he differed with them on how quickly and how firmly to press the British. Notice the neutral tone: describe the disagreement without blaming either side.

slides.heading: The Forward Bloc, May 1939
slides.body_md: A group **within the Congress** to **unite radical** members.

rows: Bring together members who wanted a bolder struggle
No settlement short of full freedom
End landlordism; reorganise agriculture and industry
Economic planning for a free India

visual.alt: Table of the Forward Bloc's objectives, paraphrased: uniting radical and anti-imperialist forces, an uncompromising struggle for complete independence, socialist reorganisation including ending landlordism, and planned development
visual.caption: Paraphrased; no text of any programme is reproduced.

slides.narration: In May nineteen thirty-nine Bose formed the Forward Bloc. At first it worked within the Congress. Its objectives were to unite all radical and anti-imperialist members, to carry on an uncompromising struggle for complete independence, and to work for a socialist reorganisation, including ending landlordism and planning the economy. Learn these in your own words.

slides.heading: Quick check: inside or outside?
slides.body_md: True or false: the Forward Bloc began as a party completely separate from the Congress.
slides.narration: Think about where the Forward Bloc began. Was it inside the Congress or completely outside it?

slides.heading: Two kinds of leadership
columns:
**Within the Congress (1938–39)**

- President at **Haripura**
- Pressed for a **firmer struggle**
- **National Planning Committee**

**After resigning (1939)**

- Formed the **Forward Bloc**
- United **radical** members
- Called for **complete independence**
slides.narration: Compare Bose's two roles in these years. As Congress President he pressed for a firmer struggle and backed economic planning. After resigning, he formed the Forward Bloc to unite those who wanted a bolder fight for complete independence. In both roles his aim was the same: full freedom, won quickly.

slides.heading: Bloc and Army compared
slides.body_md: A **political group** in India; an **army** abroad.

rows: Political group, first within the Congress

visual.alt: Comparison table: the Forward Bloc, formed in India in May 1939 as a political group first within the Congress, aimed at complete independence through political struggle with a radical programme; the Indian National Army, first formed in 1942 and led by Bose from 1943, was the army of the Provisional Government and aimed to liberate India by armed struggle
visual.caption: Two creations, two methods.

slides.narration: Do not confuse the Forward Bloc with the Indian National Army. The Bloc was a political group formed in India in nineteen thirty-nine. The army was a military force formed abroad in nineteen forty-two and led by Bose from nineteen forty-three. One worked through politics and mass action, the other through armed struggle.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: a 3-mark answer on the Bloc
slides.body_md: Explain **three objectives** of the Forward Bloc.
bullets: Objective 1: **unite** radical and anti-imperialist members.
Objective 2: an **uncompromising** struggle for **complete independence**.
Objective 3: a **socialist** programme, such as **ending landlordism** and **planning**.

rows: Bring together members who wanted a bolder struggle
No settlement short of full freedom
End landlordism; reorganise agriculture and industry
Economic planning for a free India

visual.alt: Table of the Forward Bloc's objectives, paraphrased: uniting radical and anti-imperialist forces, an uncompromising struggle for complete independence, socialist reorganisation including ending landlordism, and planned development
visual.caption: Paraphrased; no text of any programme is reproduced.

slides.narration: For a three-mark answer, give three different objectives with a short explanation each. The Bloc wanted to unite radical members, to fight without compromise for complete independence, and to reorganise society and the economy on socialist lines. Avoid writing three versions of the same point.

slides.body_md: Haripura (1938) → Tripuri (1939) → Forward Bloc (May 1939).

slides.narration: To sum up Part One. Bose left the civil service in nineteen twenty-one to join the freedom struggle. In May nineteen thirty-nine he formed the Forward Bloc to unite radical members in an uncompromising struggle for complete independence.

slides.narration: In Part Two we follow Bose abroad. He escaped from house arrest in nineteen forty-one, reached Germany, and then travelled to Southeast Asia. slides.body_md: **Calcutta** → **Peshawar and Kabul** → **Germany** → **Southeast Asia**.

visual.caption: Journey shown as a sequence, not a map.

slides.narration: In January nineteen forty-one Bose escaped from house arrest in Calcutta in disguise. He travelled through Peshawar and Kabul and reached Germany, where he organised Indian prisoners of war and broadcast messages to India. In nineteen forty-three he travelled by submarine to Southeast Asia and reached Singapore.

slides.heading: The first INA, 1942
slides.body_md: Organised by **Captain Mohan Singh** from **prisoners of war**.

slides.narration: After Japan captured Malaya and Singapore in nineteen forty-two, many Indian soldiers of the British Indian Army became prisoners. Captain Mohan Singh organised the first Indian National Army from them, with Japanese help. The Indian Independence League, led by the revolutionary Rash Behari Bose, gave it a political base among Indians in Southeast Asia.

slides.narration: In nineteen forty-three Rash Behari Bose handed over the Indian Independence League to Subhas Bose, who took command of the army and reorganised it. On the twenty-first of October nineteen forty-three he proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India at Singapore. The army was its army, and the League organised civilian support. Its brigades were named after national leaders.

slides.heading: Objectives of the INA
slides.body_md: To **free India by armed struggle**, as a **national** army.

nodes.label: Build a national army above region and religion
Win the support of Indians in Southeast Asia
Act as the army of a free Indian government

visual.alt: Flow of the INA's objectives: freeing India by armed struggle, building a national army above region and religion, winning the support of Indians in Southeast Asia, and acting as the army of a free Indian government
visual.caption: Objectives of the INA (paraphrased).

slides.narration: The army's objectives can be put simply. It aimed to free India from British rule by armed struggle. It aimed to be a truly national army, with soldiers of every region and religion serving together. It aimed to win the support of Indians in Southeast Asia. And it served as the army of the provisional government. Its slogan was Delhi Chalo.

slides.heading: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment
slides.body_md: A **women's regiment**, led by **Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan**.

slides.narration: The army included a regiment of women, named after Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, a leader of eighteen fifty-seven. It was led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan, later known as Lakshmi Sahgal. The regiment showed that women could take part in the armed struggle for freedom, and it inspired many Indians at home and abroad.

slides.body_md: Answer "Who founded the INA?" **fully** for **2 marks**.
bullets: Mark 1: **Captain Mohan Singh** organised the first INA in **1942** from **prisoners of war**, with the **Indian Independence League** of **Rash Behari Bose**.
Mark 2: **Subhas Bose** took **command** and **reorganised** it in **1943**.
Tip: some books credit **Rash Behari Bose**; naming all three roles is safest.

slides.narration: The question of who founded the army needs care. Captain Mohan Singh organised the first army in nineteen forty-two, with the support of Rash Behari Bose's Indian Independence League. Subhas Bose took command and reorganised it in nineteen forty-three. Some books credit Rash Behari Bose, so the safest answer explains all three roles.

slides.heading: The campaign of 1944
slides.body_md: **Imphal and Kohima**; flag at **Moirang**; then **retreat**.

rows: Around Imphal (Manipur) and Kohima; INA flag raised at Moirang
Supply shortages, disease, the monsoon, stronger Allied forces with air power

visual.alt: Table about the campaign of 1944: around Imphal in Manipur and Kohima, with the INA flag raised at Moirang, fought with Japanese forces, ending in retreat because of supply shortages, disease, the monsoon and stronger Allied forces with air power

slides.narration: In nineteen forty-four the army, with Japanese forces, advanced into the north-east of India around Imphal and Kohima, and its flag was raised at Moirang in Manipur. But supplies ran short, disease spread, and the heavy monsoon made movement hard, while the Allied forces were stronger and controlled the air. The campaign ended in retreat.

The circumstances have been the subject of several inquiries, so school histories describe his death as reported. Many soldiers of his army were taken prisoner and brought back to India.

slides.body_md: Three officers — **Hindu, Muslim and Sikh** — tried together.

rows: Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
Bhulabhai Desai, Jawaharlal Nehru, Tej Bahadur Sapru

visual.alt: Table about the INA trials: at the Red Fort in Delhi in 1945 and 1946; the first trial accused Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon; the defence included Bhulabhai Desai, Jawaharlal Nehru and Tej Bahadur Sapru; the sentences were remitted after nationwide protests

slides.narration: In nineteen forty-five the government put officers of the army on trial at the Red Fort in Delhi. In the first trial, Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon were tried together. They were defended by leading lawyers and leaders, including Bhulabhai Desai, Jawaharlal Nehru and Tej Bahadur Sapru.

slides.heading: Impact of the trials
slides.body_md: Support **across communities**; unrest in the **armed forces**.

nodes.label: Accused were Hindu, Muslim and Sikh
Unrest in the armed forces (naval mutiny, 1946)
Greater pressure for a transfer of power

visual.alt: Flow of the impact of the INA trials: the accused were Hindu, Muslim and Sikh, so support came from all communities; nationwide protests followed; the sentences were remitted; unrest spread to the armed forces, as in the naval mutiny of 1946; and pressure for a transfer of power grew
visual.caption: Why the trials mattered.

slides.narration: Because the accused were Hindu, Muslim and Sikh, the trials united people of every community. Meetings and protests spread across the country, and the government remitted the sentences. Sympathy also spread to Indians in the armed forces, and unrest such as the naval mutiny of nineteen forty-six followed. Britain could no longer rely on Indian troops.

- **1942:** **Captain Mohan Singh** organised the **first INA** with **Japanese** help from Indian **prisoners of war** captured in **Malaya and Singapore**.

- **Slogan:** "Delhi Chalo".
- **Objectives (paraphrased):** free India by **armed struggle**; a **national** army above region and religion; win the support of **Indians abroad**.

sections.heading: 6. The INA trials and Bose's contribution
sections.body_md:

- **Impact:** support from **every community**; nationwide protests; sentences **remitted**; unrest in the **armed forces** (naval mutiny, **1946**, as later context); greater pressure for a **transfer of power**.
- **Contribution of Bose:** radical leadership in the Congress; the **Forward Bloc**; the **INA** and the **Provisional Government**; inspiration of **armed struggle** and **national unity**; a role for **women**. **Common mistakes**
- Saying Bose founded the first INA in 1942 (it was **Mohan Singh**; Bose took command in **1943**).
- Confusing the **Forward Bloc** (political, 1939) with the **INA** (military).
- Placing the Provisional Government at **Tokyo** (it was **Singapore**).
- Stating Bose's death as certain fact (say **reported**).
- Forgetting why the trials **united** India (the accused were **Hindu, Muslim and Sikh**).

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1-mark items: one correct option or term.
- 2 marks: two distinct points.
- 10-mark questions in 3 + 3 + 4 parts: one point per mark; the 4-mark part often asks for impact or evaluation.

questions.stem_md: In which year did Subhas Chandra Bose form the Forward Bloc?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** 1939. The Forward Bloc was formed in May 1939, soon after Bose resigned as Congress President. He became President in 1938, the first INA came in 1942 and the Provisional Government in 1943.

questions.stem_md: How did the Forward Bloc first relate to the Indian National Congress when it was formed?

options.text_md: It was a rival party set up by the British government
It replaced the Congress as the main national body
It was a wing of the Muslim League
It began as a group within the Congress meant to unite its radical members

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** It began as a group within the Congress meant to unite its radical members. The Forward Bloc began as a group inside the Congress to bring together its left-wing and radical members. It was not set up by the government, it did not replace the Congress, and it had no link with the Muslim League.

questions.stem_md: At which Congress session of 1938 did Subhas Chandra Bose preside for the first time?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Haripura. Bose first presided at the Haripura session in 1938. He was re-elected for the Tripuri session of 1939; Lahore (1929) adopted complete independence; Lucknow is linked with the Pact of 1916.

questions.stem_md: Whom did Bose defeat in the contest for the Congress presidency for the Tripuri session of 1939?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Pattabhi Sitaramayya. Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, who had the backing of Gandhi and many senior leaders. Rajendra Prasad became President after Bose resigned later in 1939.

questions.stem_md: Why did Bose resign as Congress President in 1939, a few weeks after winning the election?

options.text_md: He was arrested by the British for the whole year
He had decided to leave India for Germany at once
Differences with Gandhi and senior leaders over the working committee and the pace of the struggle made it hard for him to function
The Congress session at Tripuri was cancelled

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Differences with Gandhi and senior leaders over the working committee and the pace of the struggle made it hard for him to function. Senior leaders who had backed his opponent did not cooperate in forming a working committee, and Bose differed with them on how hard to press the British, so he resigned. His arrest and departure came later (1940–41), and the Tripuri session was held.

questions.stem_md: Which of the following was an objective of the Forward Bloc?

options.text_md: To bring together all radical and anti-imperialist groups in a firm struggle for complete independence
To support British war aims in return for dominion status
To keep India out of all political activity during the war
To demand separate electorates for each community

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** To bring together all radical and anti-imperialist groups in a firm struggle for complete independence. The Bloc aimed to unite radical and anti-imperialist forces for an uncompromising struggle for complete independence. Supporting war aims, staying out of politics and separate electorates were not its aims.

questions.stem_md: Which kind of economic programme did the Forward Bloc stand for, as its objectives are usually summarised?

options.text_md: A return to rule by the princes
Free trade with no role for the state
An economy based only on cottage industries run by the British
A socialist reorganisation, including ending landlordism and planned development

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** A socialist reorganisation, including ending landlordism and planned development. The Bloc favoured a radical, socialist programme: abolishing landlordism, reorganising agriculture and industry, and planning. The other options run against its stated aims.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Bose formed the Forward Bloc in 1939.

**Reason (R):** He wanted to unite the radical elements in the Congress who favoured a firmer struggle against British rule.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Both are true, and R explains A: after resigning the presidency, Bose formed the Bloc to bring together members who wanted a stronger, uncompromising struggle.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Forward Bloc was formed with the support of the British government.

**Reason (R):** The Forward Bloc called for an uncompromising struggle against British rule.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** A is false: the Bloc opposed British rule and had no government support. R is true: it stood for a firm struggle for complete independence.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Bose was elected Congress President in two successive years, 1938 and 1939.
questions.solution_md: **True.** True. He presided at Haripura in 1938 and was re-elected for Tripuri in 1939, though he resigned the same year.

questions.stem_md: State any two objectives of the Forward Bloc formed in 1939.
questions.solution_md: Any two recognised objectives.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. To **unite all radical and anti-imperialist** elements in a firm struggle for **complete independence**.
2. To work for a **socialist** reorganisation of society and economy, including **ending landlordism** and **planned development**.

questions.stem_md: Explain why Bose's victory in the 1939 presidential election led to a crisis within the Congress.
questions.solution_md: Opposing candidate backed by senior leaders; no cooperation; resignation.

answer.model_answer_md: Bose defeated **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, who had the support of **Gandhi** and senior leaders. They **did not cooperate** in forming a **working committee** with him, and he **differed** with them on the **pace of the struggle**, so he **resigned**.

questions.stem_md: Why is Bose's decision about the Indian Civil Service seen as the start of his political career?
questions.solution_md: Passed and resigned; joined the movement.

answer.model_answer_md: He passed the **ICS examination (1920)** but **resigned in 1921**, refusing to serve the colonial government. He then joined the **national movement**, working with **C. R. Das** in Bengal.

questions.stem_md: Explain three developments of 1938–39 that led Bose to form the Forward Bloc.
questions.solution_md: Haripura; Tripuri crisis; resignation and formation.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Haripura (1938):** as President he pressed for a **firmer struggle** and **economic planning**.
2. **Tripuri (1939):** he defeated **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, the candidate backed by senior leaders, but they **did not cooperate** with him.
3. **Resignation:** he resigned in **1939** and, in **May 1939**, formed the **Forward Bloc** to unite radical members within the Congress.

questions.stem_md: Who first organised the Indian National Army in 1942 from Indian soldiers captured in Southeast Asia?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Captain Mohan Singh. Captain Mohan Singh organised the first INA in 1942, with Japanese help, from Indian prisoners of war. Bose took command in 1943; Shah Nawaz Khan was an officer later tried at the Red Fort; Bhulabhai Desai was a defence lawyer at the trials.

questions.stem_md: Which leader headed the Indian Independence League in Southeast Asia before Subhas Chandra Bose took charge?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Rash Behari Bose. Rash Behari Bose, a revolutionary living in Japan, headed the Indian Independence League and handed over its leadership to Subhas Bose in 1943. Mohan Singh led the first INA; Lakshmi Swaminathan led the women's regiment; Nehru was in India.

questions.stem_md: From whom were most of the soldiers of the first INA drawn?

options.text_md: Indian soldiers of the British Indian Army taken prisoner by the Japanese
Soldiers of the princely states inside India
British officers who opposed the war

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Indian soldiers of the British Indian Army taken prisoner by the Japanese. Most were Indian soldiers of the British Indian Army who had been captured by the Japanese in Malaya and Singapore. Indian civilians in Southeast Asia joined later.

questions.stem_md: In which year did Subhas Chandra Bose take over the leadership of the INA in Singapore?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** 1943. He reached Southeast Asia and took over the INA and the Indian Independence League in 1943. He escaped from India in 1941; the first INA was formed in 1942; the war ended in 1945.

questions.stem_md: Which of these was the main objective of the INA?

options.text_md: To help Japan rule India after the war
To defend the British Empire in Asia
To set up separate states for each community
To free India from British rule through an armed struggle

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** To free India from British rule through an armed struggle. The INA aimed to liberate India by armed struggle. It did not aim to place India under Japan, defend the Empire or divide India.

questions.stem_md: INA units were named after national leaders and drew soldiers from many regions and religions. What does this tell us about the INA's aims?

options.text_md: It recruited only from one province
It was organised on the basis of separate electorates
It was a purely religious organisation
It aimed to build a sense of national unity above region and religion

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** It aimed to build a sense of national unity above region and religion. Mixed units and names such as the Gandhi, Nehru and Azad Brigades show an aim of national unity. The INA did not recruit from one province or organise by community or religion.

questions.stem_md: What was the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA?

options.text_md: A regiment of the British Indian Army
A women's regiment led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan
A unit made up of Japanese volunteers

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** A women's regiment led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan. It was the INA's women's regiment, led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (later Sahgal). It was not a cavalry unit, a British regiment or a Japanese unit.

questions.stem_md: Where and when did Bose proclaim the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Singapore, 21 October 1943. The Provisional Government was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943. Bose was in Berlin in 1941; Tokyo and Rangoon were other centres of activity, but not the place of proclamation.

questions.stem_md: In which region did the INA, alongside Japanese forces, fight its main campaign on Indian soil in 1944?

options.text_md: Imphal and Kohima in the north-east

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Imphal and Kohima in the north-east. The 1944 campaign was fought around Imphal (Manipur) and Kohima (Nagaland region); the INA flag was raised at Moirang in Manipur. The other places were not battlegrounds of this campaign.

questions.stem_md: Which reasons are usually given for the failure of the INA's campaign of 1944?

options.text_md: Lack of support from the Indian Independence League
Shortage of supplies, the heavy monsoon and stronger Allied forces
An order from the Congress to stop fighting
The death of Bose before the campaign began

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Shortage of supplies, the heavy monsoon and stronger Allied forces. The campaign failed because of supply shortages, heavy monsoon rains, disease and stronger Allied forces with air power. The League supported the INA, the Congress gave no such order, and Bose was alive until 1945.

**Assertion (A):** Many soldiers of the first INA had earlier served in the British Indian Army.

**Reason (R):** The first INA was raised from Indian soldiers taken prisoner by the Japanese in Southeast Asia.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Both are true, and R explains A: since the INA drew on captured Indian soldiers, most of its men had served in the British Indian Army.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The INA included a regiment of women soldiers.

**Reason (R):** The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was formed by the British to guard Indian ports.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Subhas Chandra Bose personally recruited the first INA in 1942.
questions.solution_md: **False.** False. The first INA was organised by Captain Mohan Singh in 1942; Bose took over and reorganised it in 1943.

questions.stem_md: Who organised the first INA, and how was it later reorganised?
questions.solution_md: Mohan Singh in 1942; Bose in 1943.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Captain Mohan Singh** organised it in **1942** from Indian prisoners of war, with **Japanese** help and the **Indian Independence League** of **Rash Behari Bose**.
2. In **1943** **Subhas Chandra Bose** took **command**, **reorganised** it and added new units.

questions.stem_md: Mention two objectives of the Indian National Army.
questions.solution_md: Any two objectives.

answer.model_answer_md:

2. To build a **national army** that stood for **unity** across regions and religions. (Also: to **mobilise Indians abroad** for the freedom struggle.)

questions.stem_md: State two facts about the Provisional Government of Free India.
questions.solution_md: Place and date; recognition or link with the INA.

answer.model_answer_md:

questions.solution_md: Any two valid reasons.

questions.stem_md: Explain three objectives of the INA under Subhas Chandra Bose.
questions.solution_md: Three objectives, each explained.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Armed struggle:** to drive the British out of India by **military action** from the east.
2. **National unity:** to build an army in which soldiers of every **region and religion** served together, as shown by its **brigade names**.
3. **Mobilise Indians abroad:** to win the **support, money and recruits** of Indians living in **Southeast Asia** for the freedom struggle.

questions.stem_md: An imagined railway clerk in January 1941 reads that a well-known leader under police watch in his own home has vanished from the city. If the leader is Bose, which city is the clerk reading about?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** Calcutta. He escaped from house arrest in Calcutta in January 1941 and travelled through Peshawar and Kabul towards Europe.

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Germany. Bose was in Germany from 1941 to 1943, where he organised Indian prisoners of war and broadcast to India. Japan is in Asia, and the United States and Britain were fighting Germany, so Bose could not have worked there.

questions.stem_md: By which title is Subhas Chandra Bose popularly known?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Netaji. Bose is popularly known as Netaji. Lokmanya is used for Tilak, Deshbandhu for C. R. Das, and Mahatma for Gandhi.

questions.stem_md: How is the end of Bose's life usually described in school histories?

options.text_md: He was executed after the Red Fort trials
He died in prison in Mandalay
He was reported to have died in an air crash in Taipei in August 1945; the circumstances have been the subject of several inquiries
He became the first President of independent India

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** He was reported to have died in an air crash in Taipei in August 1945; the circumstances have been the subject of several inquiries. Bose was reported to have died after an air crash at Taipei (Taihoku) in August 1945, and several inquiries have since examined the circumstances. He was not tried at the Red Fort, was not in Mandalay in 1945, and did not hold office in independent India.

questions.stem_md: Where were INA officers put on trial by the British government in 1945–46?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** The Red Fort, Delhi. The INA trials were held at the Red Fort in Delhi. The other places are not linked with these trials.

options.text_md: Mohan Singh, Rash Behari Bose and Lakshmi Swaminathan
Bhulabhai Desai, Nehru and Tej Bahadur Sapru
C. R. Das, Tilak and Gokhale
Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon

Bhulabhai Desai, Nehru and Sapru were among the defence team; the others belong to different events or periods.

questions.stem_md: Why is the defence of the INA officers at the Red Fort significant for the national movement?

options.text_md: The British government paid for the defence to win Indian support
Leading Congress figures such as Bhulabhai Desai and Nehru defended them, showing nationwide support across political lines
Only the Muslim League supported the accused

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Leading Congress figures such as Bhulabhai Desai and Nehru defended them, showing nationwide support across political lines. Congress leaders, including Bhulabhai Desai and Jawaharlal Nehru, joined the defence, and support came from many parties and communities. The other options are not historical.

questions.stem_md: What was the most important effect of the INA trials on public opinion in India?

options.text_md: They aroused nationwide sympathy for the INA and strengthened the demand for freedom
They made people lose interest in the national movement
They led directly to the Partition of Bengal
They ended the Second World War

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** They aroused nationwide sympathy for the INA and strengthened the demand for freedom. The trials stirred strong public sympathy across the country and added pressure for independence. They did not reduce interest, and the Partition of Bengal (1905) and the end of the war (1945) were separate events.

questions.stem_md: Historians often say the INA trials worried the British government because of their effect on one group in particular. Which group?

The princes of the princely states

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Indian soldiers, sailors and airmen in the British forces. This was a serious concern for a government that depended on Indian soldiers.

questions.stem_md: True or false? The INA trials were held in secret, so the public knew little about them.
questions.solution_md: **False.** False. The trials at the Red Fort were widely reported and became a focus of nationwide public meetings and protests.

questions.stem_md: Mention two contributions of Subhas Chandra Bose to the freedom struggle before 1941.
questions.solution_md: Any two contributions before 1941.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. As **Congress President** (**1938**), he pressed for a **firmer struggle** and helped set up the **National Planning Committee**.
2. He formed the **Forward Bloc** (**1939**) to unite **radical** members for an **uncompromising** struggle.

questions.stem_md: Why did the INA trials become a matter of national concern rather than a military affair?
questions.solution_md: Mixed backgrounds; defence by leaders; seen as patriots.

answer.model_answer_md: The accused came from **different religions** (**Hindu, Muslim and Sikh**), so the trials **united** people across communities. Leading lawyers and leaders defended them, and the public saw the officers as **patriots**, turning the trials into a **national cause**.

questions.stem_md: Give two ways in which the INA trials affected the course of the freedom struggle.
questions.solution_md: Public sympathy; effect on the armed forces.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. They aroused **nationwide sympathy** and **united** people across communities in support of the accused.
2. They spread **unrest** among Indians in the **armed forces** (for example the **naval mutiny of 1946**), showing the British that they could no longer **rely** on Indian troops.

questions.stem_md: Explain three ways in which Bose continued the freedom struggle from outside India.
questions.solution_md: Germany; Singapore and the government; the campaign.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Germany (1941–43):** he organised **Indian prisoners of war** and **broadcast** messages to India.
2. **Southeast Asia (1943):** he took over the **INA** and the **Indian Independence League**, and proclaimed the **Provisional Government of Free India**.
3. **Military campaign (1944):** he led the INA, with Japanese forces, into the **north-east** of India around **Imphal and Kohima**.

questions.stem_md: Assess the importance of the INA trials of 1945–46 in three points.
questions.solution_md: Unity; pressure and remission; armed forces.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Unity:** the accused were **Hindu, Muslim and Sikh**, so support for them **cut across communities**.
2. **Political pressure:** leaders such as **Bhulabhai Desai** and **Nehru** defended them, and nationwide protests forced the government to **remit the sentences**.
3. **Armed forces:** sympathy spread to Indian **soldiers and sailors**, and unrest such as the **naval mutiny (1946)** showed that British rule could no longer rely on them, adding to the pressure for **independence**.

Led the Rani of Jhansi Regiment

Takes over the INA in Singapore

questions.stem_md:
Answer the following about Bose and the Forward Bloc.

(i) Describe Bose's presidency of the Congress at Haripura and his re-election for Tripuri. **[3]**
(ii) Why did he resign as President in 1939? **[3]**
(iii) When was the Forward Bloc formed, and what were its objectives? **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Haripura and Tripuri; resignation; formation and objectives.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) Bose presided at the **Haripura** session in **1938**, where he urged a **firmer struggle** and **economic planning**; the **National Planning Committee** was set up during his term. In **1939** he was **re-elected**, defeating **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, the candidate backed by **Gandhi** and senior leaders.

(ii) Senior leaders who had supported his rival **did not cooperate** in forming a **working committee**, and he **differed** with them on the **pace** of the struggle against British rule. Unable to function, he **resigned** in **1939**.

(iii) He formed the **Forward Bloc** in **May 1939**, at first **within the Congress**. Its objectives were to **unite** all **radical and anti-imperialist** elements; to carry on an **uncompromising struggle** for **complete independence**; and to work for a **socialist** reorganisation, including **ending landlordism** and **planned development**.

questions.stem_md:
Answer the following about the Indian National Army.

(i) Who organised the first INA, when, and from whom were its soldiers drawn? **[3]**
(ii) What part did Rash Behari Bose and the Indian Independence League play? **[3]**
(iii) Explain how Subhas Chandra Bose reorganised and strengthened the INA after 1943. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: First INA; League and Rash Behari Bose; reorganisation.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) **Captain Mohan Singh** organised the first INA in **1942**, with **Japanese** help, mainly from **Indian soldiers of the British Indian Army** taken prisoner after the fall of **Malaya and Singapore**.

(ii) **Rash Behari Bose**, a revolutionary living in **Japan**, led the **Indian Independence League**, which brought together **Indians in Southeast Asia** in support of the freedom struggle and provided a political base for the INA. In **1943** he **handed over** its leadership to Subhas Bose.

(iii) Subhas Bose took **command** in **1943**, **recruited** Indian **civilians** as well as soldiers, raised the **Rani of Jhansi Regiment** for women, named brigades after **Gandhi, Nehru and Azad** to stress **unity**, gave it the slogan **"Delhi Chalo"**, and placed it under the **Provisional Government of Free India**.

questions.stem_md:
Answer the following about the Provisional Government of Free India.

(i) When and where was it proclaimed, and by whom? **[3]**
(ii) Explain the link between this government and the INA. **[3]**
(iii) Describe the INA's campaign of 1944 and explain why it ended in retreat. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Who, when, where; link with the INA; campaign and retreat.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) It was proclaimed by **Subhas Chandra Bose** at **Singapore** on **21 October 1943**, and was **recognised** by **Japan** and several of its **allies**.

(ii) The **INA** was the **army** of the Provisional Government; Bose was both head of the government and **Supreme Commander** of the army, and the **Indian Independence League** organised **civilian support**, money and recruits.

(iii) In **1944** the INA, with **Japanese** forces, advanced into the **north-east** of India around **Imphal and Kohima**, and its flag was raised at **Moirang** in Manipur. It **retreated** because of **supply shortages**, **disease**, the heavy **monsoon** and the **stronger Allied forces**, which had **control of the air** as Japan began to lose the war.

questions.stem_md:
Answer the following about the contribution of Subhas Chandra Bose.

(i) Describe three of his contributions within India before 1941. **[3]**
(ii) Describe three of his contributions abroad between 1941 and 1945. **[3]**
(iii) Evaluate his overall contribution to India's freedom struggle. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Work in India; work abroad; balanced evaluation.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) He **resigned from the ICS** (**1921**) to join the movement; as **Congress President** (**1938–39**) he pressed for a **firmer struggle** and **planning**; and he formed the **Forward Bloc** (**1939**) to unite **radical** members.

(ii) In **Germany** he organised **Indian prisoners of war** and **broadcast** to India; in **1943** he took over the **INA** and proclaimed the **Provisional Government of Free India**; in **1944** he led the INA into the **north-east**.

(iii) Although the INA did not win militarily, Bose **inspired** Indians with the idea of **armed struggle** and **national unity** across **religions and regions**, gave a role to **women** in the army, and the **INA trials** that followed his campaign stirred **nationwide sympathy** and unrest in the **armed forces**, adding to the **pressure** on Britain to leave India. Historians differ on the wisdom of seeking help from the **Axis powers**; a balanced answer notes both points.

marking_scheme.step: (iii) Effect through the trials and a balanced view

questions.stem_md:
Answer the following about the INA trials.

(i) Where were the trials held, and name the three officers tried together. **[3]**
(ii) Who defended them, and how did the public react? **[3]**
(iii) Assess the impact of the trials on the British government and the freedom struggle. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Place and officers; defence and reaction; impact.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) The trials were held at the **Red Fort, Delhi**, in **1945–46**. The three officers tried together were **Shah Nawaz Khan**, **Prem Kumar Sahgal** and **Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon**.

(ii) The defence included **Bhulabhai Desai**, **Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Tej Bahadur Sapru**. There were **meetings, processions and protests** all over India; because the accused were **Hindu, Muslim and Sikh**, support came from **every community**.

(iii) Faced with this feeling, the authorities **remitted the sentences** of the three officers. Sympathy spread to Indians in the **armed forces**, and unrest such as the **naval mutiny of 1946** showed that Britain could no longer **rely** on Indian troops. The trials therefore added strong **pressure** for a **transfer of power**.

marking_scheme.step: (iii) Effect on the armed forces and on Britain

(iii) **1942:** **Mohan Singh** organised the first INA from **prisoners of war**. **1943:** Bose took command and proclaimed the **Provisional Government** at **Singapore**. **1944:** the **Imphal–Kohima** campaign ended in **retreat**. **1945:** Bose was **reported** to have died in an air crash, and INA officers were tried at the **Red Fort**, which stirred **nationwide sympathy**.

questions.stem_md: An imagined Congress member in 1939 tells his friends that he wants to join a new group inside the party that will unite those who favour a bolder fight for full freedom. Which group is he planning to join?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** The Forward Bloc. A group inside the Congress formed in 1939 to unite those favouring a bolder fight is the Forward Bloc. The Swaraj Party belongs to the 1920s, the League was a separate party, and the Indian Independence League worked in Southeast Asia.

questions.stem_md: An imagined economist in 1938 is invited to join a Congress committee that will prepare plans for industry and agriculture in a free India. During whose term as Congress President was this committee set up?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** Subhas Chandra Bose. The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938, when Bose was Congress President. The other leaders belong to earlier periods.

questions.stem_md: An imagined soldier of the British Indian Army is captured in Malaya in 1942 and is later asked to join an Indian army being formed with Japanese help. Who was organising that army at the time?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** Captain Mohan Singh. In 1942 the first INA was being organised by Captain Mohan Singh from Indian prisoners of war. Bose arrived in 1943; Mountbatten was an Allied commander; Shah Nawaz Khan was an officer.

questions.stem_md: An imagined INA recruit is posted to a brigade named after the leader who led the Salt March. Which brigade did he join?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** The Gandhi Brigade. The Salt March of 1930 was led by Gandhi, so the recruit joined the Gandhi Brigade. The Nehru and Azad Brigades honoured other leaders, and the Rani of Jhansi Regiment was the women's regiment.

questions.stem_md: An imagined young nurse in Rangoon decides in 1943 to train as a soldier for India's freedom in a unit open only to women. Which unit did she join?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** The Rani of Jhansi Regiment. The INA unit for women was the Rani of Jhansi Regiment. The Gandhi Brigade was a men's brigade, the Indian Independence League was a civilian body, and the Forward Bloc was a political group in India.

questions.stem_md: An imagined trader in Kuala Lumpur in 1943 gives jewellery and money to an organisation that supports the INA among Indians in Southeast Asia. Which organisation is this?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** The Indian Independence League. The Indian Independence League organised civilian support, funds and recruits for the INA in Southeast Asia. The other bodies worked inside India.

questions.stem_md: An imagined INA veteran recalls a hard campaign in 1944 in the hills of Manipur, with heavy rain and little food, that ended in retreat. Which campaign is he describing?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** The Imphal-Kohima campaign. A 1944 campaign in Manipur ending in retreat is the Imphal-Kohima campaign. The Dandi March and Quit India were non-violent movements, and Plassey was in 1757.

questions.stem_md: In an imagined city in late 1945, students of every community hold a joint meeting to demand the release of three army officers on trial in Delhi. Which event are they reacting to?

options.text_md: The INA trials at the Red Fort

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** The INA trials at the Red Fort. Three army officers on trial in Delhi in 1945 points to the INA trials at the Red Fort. The other events belong to different years and contexts.

questions.stem_md: An imagined naval rating in Bombay in February 1946 says that the INA trials made him question why he should serve a foreign government. Which later event is this feeling connected with?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** The naval mutiny of 1946. Unrest among Indian sailors in Bombay in February 1946 is the naval mutiny, which historians link with the feelings stirred by the INA trials. The other events are earlier.

questions.stem_md: An imagined listener in Bengal in 1942 hears a radio broadcast from Germany urging Indians to keep up the fight for freedom. Who was most likely making such broadcasts, and why was he abroad?
questions.solution_md: Bose; escape and search for support.

answer.model_answer_md: Most likely **Subhas Chandra Bose**. He had **escaped from house arrest** in Calcutta in **January 1941** and gone to **Germany** to seek **outside support** for India's freedom.

questions.stem_md: For which Congress session of 1939 was Bose re-elected President?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Tripuri. He was re-elected for the Tripuri session of 1939. Haripura (1938) was his first session as President.

questions.stem_md: True or false? When it was formed in 1939, the Forward Bloc was a party completely separate from the Congress.
questions.solution_md: **False.** False. It began as a group within the Congress to unite its radical members.

questions.stem_md: The first Indian National Army was organised in 1942 by Captain ___.
questions.solution_md: Captain Mohan Singh organised the first INA.

questions.stem_md: Who led the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan. Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (later Sahgal) led the women's regiment. The others had different roles.

questions.stem_md: True or false? The Provisional Government of Free India was proclaimed at Tokyo.
questions.solution_md: **False.** False. It was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943.

questions.stem_md: In which city were the INA officers tried in 1945–46?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Delhi. They were tried at the Red Fort in Delhi.

questions.stem_md: In which year did Bose escape from house arrest and leave India?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** 1941. He escaped in January 1941. He formed the Forward Bloc in 1939, reached Southeast Asia in 1943, and was reported dead in 1945.

questions.stem_md: The INA slogan calling its soldiers to march on the capital was "___ Chalo".
questions.solution_md: The slogan was "Delhi Chalo".
